chapter: Heroes, heard bands and Lunceford's life on the road
title: Sonny Greer in Duke Ellington's band
summary: Crawford says Greer was good only in Ellington's band and describes Freddie Jenkins and other players he noticed.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: How did -- what did you think of Sonny Greer's playing?
He was good in Duke Ellington's band. Other than that band, I never heard him in no other band. I hear him down at the -- someplace downtown playing with --
Yeah, that kind of pickup groups.
I never heard Sonny play with any other bands.
Well, how -- how -- I mean what -- what did you think about his --

Yeah, I thought a lot of it. He was playing himself. That's all I can remember. Plus Sonny, you know, he was a little guy who thought a lot of himself also, but playing in Duke Ellington's band, I don't think nobody could fit in that band, but Sonny.

Well, Duke had a different sound, different feeling, and he had a different -- had a little trumpet player in there by the name of Freddie Jenkins. Chief Whetsel Wetzsel was playing first. Freddie Jenkins, when I first saw Duke Ellington's band, I was very much impressed with Otto Hardwick Freddie Jenkins and Sonny, Orville Howard, like that. But I only looked at the drummers. Freddie Jenkins used to walk across that stage and strut. He had two fingers off his hands, (scots) and he would strut across that stage, bat-bow, strut and wind up flashing his personality, hitting the high note on the way in. He was -- he was really a showman. Yes.
